{{Short description|Stoic philosopher (fl. 225 BC)}}
{{about|the philosopher|the Roman physician, pharmacologist and botanist|Pedanius Dioscorides}}

'''Dioscorides''' ({{langx|grc|Διοσκορίδης}}, fl. 225 BC), sometimes known as '''Dioscurides''', was a [[stoicism|Stoic]] philosopher, the father of [[Zeno of Tarsus]] and a pupil of [[Chrysippus]]. All other information has been lost.<ref>{{Cite LotEP|chapter=Chrysippus}}</ref>

==Dedication==
Chrysippus dedicated the following works to Dioscorides:
* Four books on Probable Conjunctive Reasons
* Five books on the Art of Reasoning and of Modes
* A solution, according to the principles of the ancients, of the [[law of non-contradiction]]
* Five volumes of Dialectic Arguments, with no solution
* Two books on Probable Arguments bearing on Definitions
* An essay on [[Rhetoric]], spanning four books
